scope: Seeed Studio XIAO boards and selected XIAO accessories

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 Series
documents.summary: Thumb-size ESP32-S3 XIAO board. The Sense variant adds a camera expansion board, digital microphone, and microSD support for vision and audio TinyML projects.
sense_features: OV3660 camera on current Sense units
field_gotchas: Ask whether the user has the base ESP32S3, Sense, or Plus before giving camera, microphone, or B2B connector advice.
The Sense camera module changed from OV2640 to OV3660 on later units, while Seeed notes that the camera examples still apply.
Starting June 2025, Sense factory firmware may expose a default AP with SSID XIAO_ESP32S3_Sense and password seeedstudio.
Do not assume battery voltage can be read from a normal GPIO on this board.

support_notes.title: XIAO ESP32S3 Sense camera, microphone, and microSD checks
support_notes.text: For image or audio TinyML, confirm the board is the Sense variant, not the base ESP32S3. Sense hardware adds the camera expansion, PDM microphone, and microSD slot. Current Sense units may use OV3660 while older examples mention OV2640; the Seeed examples remain applicable, but users should verify their exact camera module before troubleshooting focus, frame size, or camera init failures.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3
documents.summary: Tiny ESP32-C3 XIAO board with WiFi, Bluetooth LE, 11 digital IO, 4 analog IO, UART, I2C, SPI, reset, boot button, and external antenna connector.
field_gotchas: For reliable analog reads, prefer ADC1 pins A0, A1, and A2; Seeed warns that A3/GPIO5 uses ADC2 and may be unreliable.
GPIO2, GPIO8, and GPIO9 are strapping pins. External circuits on D0, D8, or D9 can interfere with boot or upload.
If upload fails, remove external wiring from boot/strapping pins and use a known data-capable USB-C cable.

support_notes.title: XIAO ESP32C3 ADC and boot-strapping cautions
support_notes.text: For analog readings on XIAO ESP32C3, prefer ADC1 pins A0, A1, and A2. A3/GPIO5 uses ADC2 and can be unreliable. External circuitry on strapping pins GPIO2, GPIO8, or GPIO9 can also interfere with boot or upload, so remove add-ons from D0, D8, or D9 when diagnosing upload failures.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040
documents.summary: RP2040-based XIAO board with 264 KB SRAM, 2 MB flash, 11 digital pins, 4 analog pins, I2C, UART, SPI, SWD pads, boot button, reset button, and onboard RGB/user LEDs.
field_gotchas: If the serial port disappears after bad firmware, use the boot button / bootloader mode and reflash UF2 firmware.
There is no onboard radio. Do not recommend BLE, WiFi, Zigbee, or Thread without an external module.
Do not pry or lift the shield can.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 Series
documents.summary: Nordic nRF52840 XIAO board focused on Bluetooth LE. Sense variants add a PDM microphone and 6-axis IMU; Plus variants add more exposed pins and interfaces.
field_gotchas: Use the Seeed nRF52 board package for Bluetooth and low-power work.
Use the mbed-enabled package when the user needs embedded ML, IMU, or PDM microphone support.
To read battery voltage safely, set P0.14 LOW to enable the divider before reading P0.31; do not leave P0.14 HIGH during a battery read.
Sense-only sensors should not be promised for the base nRF52840 board.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO nRF52840 Series

support_notes.title: XIAO nRF52840 battery and Sense package guidance
support_notes.text: For battery voltage on XIAO nRF52840, enable the divider by driving P0.14/READ_BAT_ENABLE low, then read P0.31/AIN7_BAT. Use the mbed-enabled board package when the project needs Sense IMU or PDM microphone support, and do not promise those sensors on the base nRF52840 board.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO SAMD21
documents.summary: Original XIAO board formerly named Seeeduino XIAO, based on Microchip SAMD21G18. It has 11 digital/analog pins, 10 PWM pins, one DAC output on D0, I2C, UART, SPI, SWD pads, and USB-C.
field_gotchas: D0 is the DAC-capable pin; do not imply that every analog-capable pin can output true analog voltage.
If the port disappears after a bad upload, double-short the RST pads to enter bootloader mode.
There is no onboard radio. Wireless projects need an external module.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C6
documents.summary: ESP32-C6 XIAO board with WiFi 6, Bluetooth LE, Zigbee, Thread, and Matter-oriented smart-home use. It exposes the XIAO D0-D10 pattern plus RF switch control pins.
field_gotchas: For external antenna use, set GPIO3 LOW to activate RF switch control, then set GPIO14 HIGH to select the external antenna.
GPIO14 LOW is the default built-in ceramic antenna selection.
This is the best fit in this corpus for Thread, Zigbee, and Matter questions.
Ask whether the user's framework supports ESP32-C6 Zigbee/Thread for their exact runtime before promising library compatibility.

support_notes.title: XIAO ESP32C6 RF switch and battery-voltage checks
support_notes.text: To select the external U.FL antenna on XIAO ESP32C6, enable RF switch control with GPIO3 low, then set GPIO14 high. GPIO14 low selects the onboard ceramic antenna. For battery-voltage measurement, treat the battery read circuitry separately from normal analog pins and follow the board-specific example.

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO RA4M1
documents.summary: Renesas RA4M1 XIAO board using the R7FA4M1AB3CNE Arm Cortex-M4 MCU up to 48 MHz. It adds expanded rear IO, CAN bus, a 14-bit ADC, 12-bit DAC, EEPROM, RGB LED, and battery-voltage measurement support.
field_gotchas: RA4M1 has no onboard radio; wireless projects require an external module or a different XIAO family.
Battery-voltage reading uses BAT_DET_PIN/P105 and must be enabled with BAT_READ_EN/P400 high.
Use the Seeed Renesas board package URL in Arduino IDE for board support.
RA4M1 is a good fit when a project needs CAN bus, DAC output, EEPROM, or expanded IO rather than WiFi/BLE.

support_notes.title: XIAO RA4M1 battery voltage read path
support_notes.text: XIAO RA4M1 can read battery voltage without the manual resistor workaround required by some earlier XIAO boards. Read BAT_DET_PIN/P105, but first set BAT_READ_EN/P400 high to enable the battery measurement path.

support_notes.title: XIAO RA4M1 Arduino package setup
support_notes.text: For Arduino IDE, add the Seeed Renesas board package URL, install the Seeed Renesas board support, then select the XIAO RA4M1 board before uploading a blink or serial test.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO RA4M1

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO MG24 Series
documents.summary: Silicon Labs EFR32MG24 XIAO board with Arm Cortex-M33 at 78 MHz, 256 KB RAM, 1536 KB flash plus 4 MB onboard flash, strong 2.4 GHz RF, Matter/Thread/Zigbee/BLE support, and a Sense variant with analog microphone and 6-axis IMU.
field_gotchas: MG24 Sense has the microphone and 6-axis IMU; the base MG24 does not.
The 5V pin can be used as voltage input only with suitable diode protection between the external source and 5V pin.
Deep sleep / EM4 can make the board difficult to reprogram; use the documented escape pin or recovery scripts before experimenting heavily.
MG24 is a strong pick for Matter, Thread, Zigbee, and Bluetooth mesh projects where low power matters.

support_notes.title: XIAO MG24 deep sleep recovery and bricking prevention
support_notes.text: XIAO MG24 can become difficult to upload to after deep sleep experiments. Seeed documents using PC1 pulled low during reset as an escape mechanism, and provides flash erase recovery scripts for Windows and macOS. Avoid deploying deep sleep sketches without an escape path.

support_notes.title: XIAO MG24 Sense sensor distinction
support_notes.text: Only XIAO MG24 Sense includes the onboard analog microphone and 6-axis IMU. Ask for the exact variant before giving microphone, IMU, or onboard ML sensor advice.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO MG24

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO nRF54L15 Series
documents.summary: Next-generation Nordic nRF54L15 XIAO board with 128 MHz Arm Cortex-M33 plus 128 MHz RISC-V coprocessor, Bluetooth LE 6.0 with channel sounding, Matter, Thread, Zigbee, NFC, and a Sense variant with IMU and microphone.
field_gotchas: Use nRF Connect SDK / Zephyr style workflows for advanced nRF54L15 development rather than assuming classic Arduino-only workflows.
Sense-only IMU and microphone should not be promised for the base nRF54L15 board.
nRF54L15 is the best fit in this corpus for Bluetooth 6.0 channel sounding or newer Nordic multiprotocol work.
Battery powered designs can use the internal PMIC and AIN7_VBAT battery voltage path.

support_notes.title: XIAO nRF54L15 wireless protocol selection
support_notes.text: Choose XIAO nRF54L15 when the design needs Nordic BLE 6.0 features such as channel sounding, NFC, Matter, Thread, Zigbee, or high-throughput 2.4 GHz proprietary modes. For simpler BLE-only projects, XIAO nRF52840 may be easier.

support_notes.title: XIAO nRF54L15 Sense sensor distinction
support_notes.text: XIAO nRF54L15 Sense adds the LSM6DS3TR-C 6-axis IMU and MSM261DGT006 microphone. Confirm Sense vs base before recommending onboard motion or audio examples.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO nRF54L15(Sense)

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5
documents.summary: ESP32-C5 XIAO board with 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz dual-band WiFi 6, Bluetooth 5 LE / mesh, 8 MB PSRAM, 8 MB flash, battery charge management, external RF antenna, and 11 XIAO GPIO pins.
field_gotchas: Choose ESP32-C5 when dual-band 2.4/5 GHz WiFi 6 matters; choose ESP32-C6 for Thread/Zigbee/Matter 802.15.4 work.
Reserve JTAG pins MTMS, MTDI, MTCK, and MTDO during deep sleep experiments to avoid making firmware flashing harder.
Battery-voltage reading uses GPIO6 for BAT_VOLT_PIN and GPIO26 for BAT_VOLT_PIN_EN.
The serial port may disappear during deep sleep and reappear after wake-up.

support_notes.title: XIAO ESP32-C5 dual-band WiFi guidance
support_notes.text: Use XIAO ESP32-C5 when a project needs 5 GHz WiFi or dual-band WiFi 6 in the XIAO form factor. It is not the same choice as ESP32-C6, which is better for Thread/Zigbee/802.15.4.

support_notes.title: XIAO ESP32-C5 battery voltage read path
support_notes.text: For battery voltage on XIAO ESP32-C5, enable the measurement circuit through GPIO26/BAT_VOLT_PIN_EN, then read GPIO6/BAT_VOLT_PIN. Keep the measurement range and voltage divider behavior in mind.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5

documents.title: Seeed Studio XIAO RP2350
documents.summary: RP2350-based XIAO board with dual Arm Cortex-M33 at 150 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, 2 MB flash, RGB LED, 19 multifunction GPIOs, expanded rear IO, secure boot / TrustZone features, and direct battery voltage measurement.
field_gotchas: There is no onboard radio. Wireless projects need an external module or a wireless XIAO variant.
Use the arduino-pico core version 4.2.0 or later for Arduino support.
Enter BOOT mode by holding Boot while plugging in USB, or by holding Boot, clicking Reset, then releasing Boot.
RP2350 has more IO than RP2040 and supports direct battery-voltage measurement on GPIO29.

support_notes.title: XIAO RP2350 boot mode and recovery
support_notes.text: For upload or recovery on XIAO RP2350, enter BOOT mode by holding Boot while plugging in the USB cable, or while connected by holding Boot, pressing Reset, then releasing Boot. Then select the port and upload known-good firmware.

support_notes.title: XIAO RP2040 vs RP2350 choice
support_notes.text: Choose RP2350 over RP2040 when you need dual Cortex-M33 performance, more SRAM, expanded rear IO, security features such as secure boot / TrustZone, or direct battery voltage measurement.

citations.title: Getting Started with Seeed Studio XIAO RP2350(Arduino)

documents.title: XIAO W5500 Ethernet Adapter
documents.summary: A compact Ethernet / PoE adapter around XIAO ESP32S3 Plus and W5500. It supports wired Ethernet examples using ESP32 Arduino Ethernet APIs, with SPI wiring to the XIAO pins and optional PoE power.
field_gotchas: The adapter examples target XIAO ESP32S3 Plus / ESP32 Arduino Ethernet APIs, not every XIAO board.
If using a non-PoE Ethernet cable, power the XIAO separately through a stable 5V USB-C supply.
For Ethernet bring-up, watch serial output for ETH start, link, DHCP IP, duplex, and link speed events.
Use D1 as chip select and D8/D9/D10 for SPI unless adapting the example carefully.

support_notes.title: XIAO W5500 Ethernet debug checklist
support_notes.text: For no Ethernet link, verify cable quality, switch/router link lights, PoE vs non-PoE power path, SPI pins D8/D9/D10, chip select D1, and serial event logs. After DHCP succeeds, the serial monitor should show the MAC address and assigned IPv4 address.

citations.title: Getting Started with XIAO W5500 Ethernet Adapter
